JSON: Name: gpo_preoptimization Title: Continuous-time local Gaussian process pre-optimization for efficient asynchronous event-inertial odometry Short Hypothesis: Introducing a two-step local temporal Gaussian process pre-optimization that converts raw IMU measurements into pseudo-measurement trajectories and propagates analytic Jacobians yields lower trajectory estimation error and reduced backend optimization time (constant-time query and linear preintegration cost) than existing global-temporal-GP and discrete-time preintegration methods for asynchronous event-inertial odometry. Related Work: Prior work on inertial preintegration and continuous-time state estimation splits into three families. Discrete-time IMU preintegration methods provide compact relative-motion factors between keyframes but ignore intra-interval high-frequency motion and rely on piecewise-constant assumptions, which degrades accuracy with asynchronous measurements. Differential-equation and continuous-time approaches model motion more faithfully but impose heavy initialization and online inference costs and make querying and backend integration more expensive. Gaussian-process (GP) based approaches model IMU signals as latent stochastic processes; global temporal-GP methods support fully asynchronous fusion but create large numbers of inertial factors and high computational expense, while latent-GP preintegration variants reduce modeling complexity but require multiple independent GPs, expensive numerical Jacobian computation, or reintegration when biases change. Event-inertial odometry pipelines either convert events to synchronous frame-like associations and use discrete preintegration or adopt continuous-time trajectory models with high backend cost. Unresolved issues include inefficient querying of pseudo-measurements and Jacobians at arbitrary timestamps, high preintegration/query computational complexity, and sensitivity to initialization or linearization errors. Abstract: This work addresses efficient tightly-coupled fusion of fully asynchronous event streams and high-rate inertial measurements for ego-motion estimation. We propose a continuous-time local Gaussian Process pre-optimization (GPO) that converts raw IMU streams within each integration period into a compact local temporal-GP pseudo-measurement trajectory using a light-weight two-step optimization. GPO analytically propagates procedural Jacobians from stored discrete pseudo-states to arbitrary query times, enabling constant-time queries of preintegrated rotation, velocity, translation, their covariances, and bias derivatives. The method supports asynchronous event feature projection factors by supplying accurate continuous-time inertial constraints without embedding large global GP states in the backend. The main contributions are (1) a local TGP pre-optimization to represent IMU measurements as pseudo-measurement trajectories, (2) analytic Jacobian propagation for arbitrary-time queries, and (3) an end-to-end asynchronous event-inertial odometry pipeline demonstrating linear preintegration cost and constant query cost. We expect improved estimation accuracy and reduced backend computational load compared to global-GP and discrete preintegration baselines for aggressive and HDR motion scenarios. Experiments: Datasets: (1) Simulated IMU+motion simulator with ground-truth pose to control integration duration, gyroscope and accelerometer noise, and bias profiles. (2) Public event-inertial datasets: DAVIS240C, UZH-FPV, VECtor, HKU-Stereo, DSEC. (3) Own-collected dataset with DVXplorer (640x480) mounted on a quadrotor with Optitrack (indoor) and RTK (outdoor) ground truth. Baselines: discrete-time preintegration (standard IMU preintegration), latent-process preintegration (LPM), GP-preintegration with multiple independent GPs (GPP), global temporal-GP trajectory regression (global TGP), and state-of-the-art event-inertial pipelines (DEVO, USLAM, ESVO variants) when applicable. Metrics: Mean Position Error (MPE, percent of trajectory length), rotation RMSE (Crmse, deg), Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE), preintegration time (ms) vs integration duration, query time for pseudo-measurements/Jacobians (ms per query), memory footprint (MB), and robustness measures: failure rate and error statistics under varying IMU noise and bias drift. Experimental setup and protocol: (A) Simulation: for each noise level (gyro std ∈ {1e-5,1e-4,1e-3,0.02,0.05} rad/s; accel std ∈ {1e-5,1e-4,1e-3,0.025,0.05} m/s^2) run 100 randomized motion trials; measure ∆C, ∆v, ∆r errors for integration durations ∈ {0.05,0.1,0.5,1.0,2.0}s; compare Jacobian-corrected reintegration vs propagated Jacobians. (B) Public datasets: run each method with identical frontend feature associations where possible; align trajectories using SE(3) for stereo methods and SIM(3) for monocular baselines; report MPE and Crmse per sequence averaged over ≥10 runs; record per-frame/back-end optimization time and per-query time. (C) Own-collected data: evaluate robustness under aggressive flight profiles; report Crmse and MPE per sequence. Ablations: (1) remove two-step pre-optimization (use direct GP regression over same window); (2) vary K sampling points per preintegration window (e.g., K ∈ {3,5,9,17}) and report accuracy vs compute; (3) compare analytic Jacobian propagation to numerical reintegration for bias updates; (4) scale sliding-window size in backend to test computational scaling. Statistical tests: report mean, median, standard deviation, and 95% confidence intervals across trials; test pairwise performance differences using Wilcoxon signed-rank test (alpha=0.05). Implementation notes: measure CPU-only runtimes on a fixed machine; fix frontend processing budgets and identical optimization tolerances across methods. Risk Factors and Limitations: Approximation and linearization errors: the method linearizes rotation about stored local TGP states and assumes biases constant within integration windows; these approximations can introduce systematic bias under highly non-smooth or impulsive motion (large jerk) or rapidly time-varying biases. Sampling and model choice sensitivity: performance depends on the number and placement of discrete pseudo-state samples (K) and GP prior hyperparameters; under-sampling leads to bias, over-sampling increases compute and memory. Initialization and convergence: the two-step pre-optimization may fail or converge to poor local minima when events are extremely sparse or when initial bias estimates are far from true values. Real-time constraints and frontend latency: while query cost is constant, serial event-by-event frontend processing can produce latency that violates real-time requirements when event rates are very high unless parallelized. Dataset and evaluation bias: public datasets may favor motion patterns compatible with the chosen GP prior (e.g., smooth motion), limiting generalization to other domains. Scalability and memory: storing procedural Jacobians for many windows increases memory footprint for long trajectories or large sliding windows. Sensor-model mismatch: the method assumes IMU noise is well-modelled as Gaussian white noise on jerk; non-Gaussian or correlated sensor disturbances will degrade covariance estimates and downstream optimization. Failure modes: divergence when bias drift exceeds window assumptions, degraded accuracy when event features are unreliable (low texture or lighting), and inability to recover scale in strictly monocular setups without external scale observability.
